_about: Content for one JP Race Day Programme edition. Layout lives in raceday/template.html; build with: python3 tools/build_raceday.py raceday/2026-united-states. Fields set to null are race-weekend information that must be filled in (and verified) before the build will produce a final, publishable PDF. Every figure carries a 'kind': verified (official/primary source), measured (computed from published timing data), estimate (sourced estimate with stated assumptions) or analysis (JP Motorsport Journal's editorial view).

cover.headline: Who finishes second?
cover.standfirst: The title is Kimi Antonelli's. Behind him, 16 points cover Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell and Leclerc with four races left, and Mercedes can wrap up the Constructors' at Interlagos.
cover.photo_note: Free-licensed photo pending (Wikimedia Commons is blocked in the build environment). Until then the cover uses the circuit outline.

intro: Antonelli clinched the championship in Mexico City with third place, the youngest champion in Formula 1 history. Verstappen's win there lifted him to second, two points ahead of Hamilton. Interlagos is a standard weekend this year: three practice sessions, qualifying on Saturday and the 71-lap race on Sunday, on a track where the weather and the Safety Car often have the final say.

storylines.title: Four drivers, 16 points
storylines.text: Verstappen (261), Hamilton (259), Russell (250) and Leclerc (245) are fighting to finish runner-up to Antonelli, with 100 points left.

storylines.title: Mercedes' title point
storylines.text: Mercedes lead Ferrari by 126 in the Constructors'. Outscore Ferrari by four points or more on Sunday and the teams' title is theirs too.
storylines.basis: Constructors' standings after Round 19: Mercedes 630, Ferrari 504. After São Paulo, three races remain, worth at most 43 points each to a team (25 + 18), so 129 in total. A lead of 130 or more after Sunday is decisive.

storylines.title: Expect the unexpected
storylines.text: Formula 1 puts the chance of a Safety Car here at 86%, based on the last seven races, and Interlagos weather can turn in minutes.

circuit.overtaking_aids_note: Active aero Straight Mode works in FIA-designated activation zones, and Overtake Mode gives a car within one second of the car ahead at the detection point extra electrical energy. Interlagos's zones come in the FIA event notes on race weekend and go into the final edition.
circuit.map_note: Numbered: corners confirmed from the official outline; full numbering pending a check against the FIA map.

key_sections.name: The Senna S
key_sections.text: Turn 1 drops sharply downhill and left, straight into the right of Turn 2. It is the main overtaking spot at the start of a lap and the scene of many first-lap collisions.

key_sections.name: Reta Oposta
key_sections.text: After Curva do Sol, the back straight runs down to Turn 4, Descida do Lago: the second big braking zone and the next chance to pass.

key_sections.name: The infield
key_sections.text: A slow, twisting run of corners through the middle of the lap. It is hard to pass here, so drivers aim for a clean exit before the climb.

key_sections.name: Junção and the climb
key_sections.text: Junção, the last slow corner, opens a long, flat-out uphill run past the pits to Turn 1. A good exit is worth a tow all the way to the Senna S.

circuit.time_gain_loss: The lap hinges on Junção: get out of it well and the long climb carries the car into the Senna S with a chance to pass.
circuit.dek: Fifteen corners, anticlockwise, up and down a natural bowl: the Senna S, the Reta Oposta, a twisting infield and the long climb past the pits.

pit_loss_notes: Time in the pit lane is measured: the median from pit entry to pit exit at Interlagos was 23.2–24.0 s in 2019, 2022, 2023 and 2025 (f1db timing data); the wet, red-flagged 2024 race skews it. It does not change under a VSC or Safety Car because the pit-lane speed limit still applies.
Net race-time loss is what a stop costs compared with staying out. Formula 1's 2025 preview put it at about 20.8 s here.

The VSC and Safety Car figures apply published estimates of the saving (roughly 17–40% under a VSC and 35–60% behind the Safety Car) to that 20.8 s. They are illustrative ranges, not Interlagos measurements.

strategy.history_note: Interlagos rarely runs to plan: weather, Safety Cars and red flags have shaped each of the last three races.
strategy.tyres: Pirelli has nominated C3 (hard), C4 (medium) and C5 (soft), the softest three in its range and one step softer than last year.
strategy.tyre_plan_note: the predicted race strategies (one stop or two, and in which compound order), each with its pit window on a lap chart, plus the undercut and pace gaps where Pirelli publishes them after qualifying.
strategy.one_vs_two: Last year's softer-than-usual race was mostly two stops, and this year's tyres are a step softer again. With an 86% Safety Car chance, teams will keep their options open and react to neutralisations rather than commit early.
strategy.undercut: Undercut: pit first and use the new tyres' extra grip to gain the time you lose in the pit lane before your rival stops. It works best when new tyres are much faster than worn ones.
strategy.overcut: Overcut: stay out longer and gain time on a clear track while your rival is held up on cold new tyres or in traffic. It works best when tyres warm up slowly or the pitting car rejoins in traffic.
strategy.pit_window: In 2025, the top 10's stops came between laps 7 and 54 of 71, with the first wave around laps 17–21.
strategy.neutralisation: A VSC or Safety Car inside the pit window makes a stop cheaper for everyone, so the leaders often pit together and little changes. The real swing comes when it falls just before a team's planned stop, or when a rival has already stopped under green. A Safety Car early in the race can make a one-stop too long and force a second stop.
what_to_watch: The start into the Senna S. The downhill Turn 1 is the best place to gain, and to lose, positions on lap one.
Safety Car timing. With an 86% chance of one, a neutralisation can turn a two-stop race on its head.
Mercedes against Ferrari. Four more points than Ferrari on Sunday and the Constructors' title is settled.

briefing.grid_note: The official starting grid, including penalties and any driver substitutions, is added in the final edition after qualifying.
five_things: The start into the Senna S, downhill and left: the best chance of the lap to gain places, and the riskiest.
The fight for second. Two points split Verstappen and Hamilton, with Russell and Leclerc within 16.
Mercedes' Constructors' title. Outscore Ferrari by four points or more and it is settled with three races to spare.
Safety Cars and weather. Formula 1 puts the Safety Car chance at 86%; watch the skies above the grandstands.
Antonelli's first race as champion, at the track where he took second place last year.
glossary: Pitting before a rival to use new tyres' extra pace to get ahead when they stop.
Staying out longer than a rival to gain time while they warm up new tyres or sit in traffic.
The range of laps when a stop makes strategic sense.
How quickly a tyre loses grip and lap time as it wears.
Virtual Safety Car: everyone must slow to a set pace; positions are frozen and no one may overtake.
A physical car leads the field at reduced speed, bunching everyone up behind it.
2026 active aero: wings flatten to cut drag in designated zones. Replaces DRS.
Extra electrical energy for a car within one second of the car ahead at the detection point.
From qualifying until the race, cars cannot be changed without a penalty.
